analysis.title: GS Miller - [GSX] Global Reflections 16 Oct 2026
key_insights: AI credit spreads (GSUCHS30) and hyperscaler spreads (GSXUHYPR) are at the widest levels of the year. The last time spreads were nearly this wide, the underlying equities were 15% lower.
The desk says AI capex has likely peaked. The debate has moved to financing, sustainability and returns on capital, away from near-term earnings revisions.
Sentiment is more pessimistic and breadth is low. Put volume on 16 Oct was the second highest on record for the desk's series, behind June 2026.
The desk's call to focus on non-AI trades has worked. It does not treat skepticism and uncertainty as overvaluation: the NDX trades at 21x earnings and AI multiples reflect the uncertainty.
Investors are weighing AI growth risks against a hotter-for-longer inflation backdrop ahead of the midterms. Financial conditions (FCI) have shifted from a positive to a negative driver of growth.

Beta-adjusted net exposure is at the 67th percentile over 5 years, above net leverage at the 17th percentile. Sector, factor, neutral beta (GSP1BETA) is down 15%. Cyclicals vs defensives ex commodities (GSP1CYDE) implies 2% growth, down from 6% at the highs.
The market is absorbing stress through rotation rather than index-level weakness, despite rising correlations and crowded positioning. The desk believes the broadening trade has room to run.

Call 1, buy the broadening: SPXXAI has outperformed the S&P 500 by 586bps since Oct 6. Concerns about AI debt financing and earnings growth are likely to persist, particularly as China's AI capacity ramp challenges the US AI bottleneck thesis.

Europe has less AI concentration but is increasingly correlated with the US AI trade. The preferred European broadening trade is the ex-Secular Themes basket (GSXESXXX), up about 4.5% since Oct 1 vs a flat STOXX 600.

Call 2, quality comeback: the Quality Pair Index (GSP1QUAL) is up 20% over 3 months to a 12-month high on about 13% realized vol. The short leg (GSX1BFQS) sold off as higher rates hurt long-duration, highly levered and unprofitable companies. RSI above 80 implies scope for a sharp reversal if inflation/rates concerns ease.
European quality (GSPEQUAL) has lagged the US but is catching up. The L/S pair returned +7.5% in the last month, and Europe's weaker growth/inflation mix suggests further room.

Call 3, defensive mid-term trade: Healthcare outperformed this week on a defensive bid. The preferred trade is long ACA-exposed beneficiaries (GSHLCACA), on the Democratic push to revive enhanced ACA premium tax credits that expired at end-2025.
Reauthorizing the ACA subsidies would likely return patient volumes to providers that now face higher bad debt and uncompensated care as patients move to self-pay.

Call 4, Brazil as an uncorrelated trade into Oct 25: valuations are near mid-cycle, foreign participation is below prior election-cycle peaks, and positioning in rate-sensitive domestic equities (GSBZRATE) is light. The desk sees the complex moving from mid-teens to high-teens P/E.

Call 5, Taiwan AI hedges: TSMC fell 2.3% on a full-year guidance raise and accelerated capacity buildout, which the desk reads as weak appetite to buy AI on a demand narrative. Taiwan positioning is at record levels and earnings are not meeting very high expectations.
The Asia team published a menu of tactical Taiwan tech hedges, including shorts on Taiwan Semis (GSXATWSM) and Taiwan Tech ex TSMC (GSXATTXT).
AI beneficiaries vs the rest of the market are down 25% from their highs. No pocket of AI except productivity was spared this week.

market_movers.rationale: TSMC fell 2.3% despite a full-year guidance raise and faster capacity buildout. The desk reads this as weak appetite to buy AI on a demand narrative, and recommends tactical Taiwan tech hedges.

sector_views.rationale: A defensive bid lifted the sector this week. The desk prefers long ACA-exposed beneficiaries ahead of the midterms on possible revival of enhanced ACA premium tax credits.
Credit spreads are at the widest of the year, capex growth has likely peaked, and the debate has moved to financing and returns on capital.
The Quality Pair Index is up 20% in 3 months, driven by a selloff in long-duration, levered and unprofitable names as rates rose. RSI above 80 signals reversal risk.
Valuations are near mid-cycle, foreign participation is below prior election-cycle peaks and positioning is light, led by financials, capital markets, small caps and domestic cyclicals.

earnings_insights: TSMC raised full-year guidance and accelerated its capacity buildout, and the stock fell 2.3% (figure as stated in the report, date not specified).
The desk says hyperscaler capex growth has likely peaked y/y and its impact on earnings has as well.

tension_points.bull_case: Nominal growth is holding up, employment is strong, and valuations have compressed (NDX at 21x). The desk expects rotation into non-AI names to continue rather than a broad equity meltdown.
tension_points.bear_case: AI credit spreads are at the year's widest. Last time, hyperscaler equities were 15% lower. Capex growth has likely peaked, and financial conditions, inflation and crowded positioning add risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Quality reversal risk if inflation/rates concerns ease, given RSI above 80 on the quality pair.
